changes.what: "November 1, 2026, is the anticipated start date for [SEWP VI](#term:sewp) request submissions." [544](#cite:544) SEWP V contracts are extended through January 31, 2027, and the SEWP VI period of performance runs November 1, 2026 through October 31, 2036 [542](#cite:542). The FAQ counts over 2,115 prime contract holders, including more than 1,300 small businesses [544](#cite:544). SECONDARY ONLY: awards were announced June 23, 2026 [545](#cite:545). Whether SEWP moves to [GSA](#term:gsa) under [Executive Order](#term:executive-order) 14240 is not stated on any page read [509](#cite:509) [542](#cite:542).

NOT CONFIRMED AS LIVE on October 3, 2026, and not to be shown as open: [AFWERX](#term:afwerx) Prime, whose latest dated primary source found is January 30, 2024 [1303](#cite:1303); NavalX Tech Bridges, NavalX having been consolidated into the Naval Rapid Capabilities Office (chg-navalx-into-nrco) [1280](#cite:1280); the Blue UAS Cleared List, moved to DCMA effective December 3, 2025 (chg-blue-uas-to-dcma) [1288](#cite:1288); [DHS](#term:agency-abbreviations) SVIP, whose page is dated April 19, 2024 and listed no open topic calls [1311](#cite:1311); NASA Tipping Point, whose most recent selection found is dated July 25, 2023 [1344](#cite:1344); the NSF Convergence Accelerator, whose page lists funding opportunities posted March 2020 and December 2021 without saying whether either is open [1398](#cite:1398); and the USSOCOM SOF AT&L [CSO](#term:cso), known from an aggregator copy of a [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) notice only (SECONDARY, gated on recheck) [1295](#cite:1295). This entry records a verification state, not a change in law.

A second set of four FAR-overhaul [proposed rules](#term:proposed-rule) was issued September 18, 2026, comments due October 19, 2026: Parts 8, 12, 13, 15, 38, 44 and 51 ([FAR](#term:far) Case 2026-003, 91 [FR](#term:federal-register) 59406); Parts 16, 17 and 35 (FAR Case 2026-006); Parts 9, 27 and 47; and Parts 14, 28 and 36, with Part 52 [clauses](#term:clause-numbering) [409](#cite:409) [405](#cite:405) [406](#cite:406) [521](#cite:521). [SBA](#term:sba) Advocacy calls them "the second of four planned sets" [409](#cite:409). FAR Case 2026-003 would move [micro-purchase](#term:micro-purchase-threshold) procedures from subpart 13.2 to subpart 12.4, keep simplified commercial procedures up to $9 million ($15 million for specified emergencies), remove provisions 52.212-3 and 52.212-5, require agencies to use existing contracts designated required use or best in class before soliciting new ones, and remove Part 38 [405](#cite:405) [521](#cite:521). FAR Case 2026-006 would give unsuccessful offerors on orders above the [simplified acquisition threshold](#term:simplified-acquisition-threshold) up to $7.5 million a brief explanation on written request, and Part 15 debriefing procedures above $7.5 million [406](#cite:406). The Federal Register search of October 3, 2026 returned no [Part 19](#term:far-part-19) proposed rule and no [final rule](#term:final-rule) [407](#cite:407).

[Pub. L.](#term:public-law) 119-106, the Stop Secret Spending Act of 2025 (enactment date as extracted by the fetch), amends the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act so that [other transaction agreements](#term:other-transaction) are reported on [USAspending.gov](#term:usaspending): a compilation report within 1 year; "data relating to other transaction agreements is automatically transmitted to the website" within 3 years; an implementation plan to Congress within 2 years if not compliant; [inspector general](#term:dod-ig) reports within 1 year and at least every 2 years for 10 years [1421](#cite:1421). [GAO](#term:gao) had found over $40 billion in OTAs not reported to USAspending.gov [1129](#cite:1129).

[SBA](#term:sba) proposed on June 11, 2026 (91 [FR](#term:federal-register) 35433, RIN 3245-AI75; comments due July 13, 2026) [313](#cite:313) and made final on August 11, 2026 (91 FR 51568) the removal of the [rebuttable presumption](#term:disadvantage) of social disadvantage in 13 [CFR](#term:cfr) 124.103 for individually owned [8(a)](#term:eight-a) applicants: "This rule is effective on September 10, 2026. It applies to all pending applications of individually-owned applicants as of that date." [314](#cite:314) "It does not in any way amend or affect the eligibility of [entity-owned](#term:entity-owned-firm) small businesses." [314](#cite:314) Social disadvantage remains a one-time determination, so individuals already found disadvantaged need not re-establish it [314](#cite:314). The [eCFR](#term:ecfr) text of 124.103 carries the new test [312](#cite:312). On the effective date SBA returned pending individually owned applications with 45 calendar days to resubmit and gave priority to ten [NAICS codes](#term:naics) [325](#cite:325).
